newsitem.title: USA: Regional Bells cooperate on unified Yellow Pages.
newsitem.headline: Regional Bells cooperate on unified Yellow Pages.

text.p: Four regional Bell companies said Wednesday they have banded together in an effort to bring some order to the chaos that dominates telephone directory services over the Internet.

The four -- U S West Communications Goup, BellSouth, SBC Communications Inc.'s Pacific Bell unit, and Ameritech Corp. -- said they have developed a shared Yellow Pages directory service that links existing individual regional and local directories through a common "jump page."

Consumers browsing the Internet in search of a particular phone number -- business or residential -- can access each participant's individual directory by selecting the appropriate state on a map of the United States that is linked to ads placed on high-traffic web sites, the companies said.

At present, directory services over the Internet are "very spotty, very hit or miss," said Bill Bass, of Forrester Research. Current services can frustrate Internet users just looking for the number of a local plumber, for instance.
"It is the case that this is a very shoddy market place," Bass said. "Most directories out there are fairly worthless on the local level."

Bass said an approach such as that taken by the four participants makes greater sense than other efforts now under way to build a single national directory. The national approach is likely to "fail abysmally," he said, because "It's like trying to boil the ocean."
The collective effort also provides the participants with an advertising presence on highly trafficked web sites that was not worth pursuing individually, they said.
"It allows us to enjoy some economies of purchasing national advertising that our competitors enjoy," said Dan Finnigan, executive director for business development at Pacific Bell Interactive Media.
Each of the participating Baby Bells is contributing a minimum of "several hundred thousand dollars," principally to pay for the advertising, Finnigan said.
